context: Steam reviews of ELEX, a single-player open-world action role-playing game
procedure: embedding clustering → LLM naming → test by two coders → merge of inseparable sub-themes / LLM revision

STORYTELLING.name: Factions and Lore
STORYTELLING.definition: This sub-theme encompasses the narrative elements related to the game's factions, including their ideologies, lore, and the player's choices regarding joining or interacting with them. It distinguishes itself from other sub-themes by focusing specifically on the narrative depth and complexity of faction-related content, rather than general world-building or character development.

STORYTELLING.name: Narrative Quality
STORYTELLING.definition: This sub-theme addresses the overall quality of the game's writing, including dialogue, plot, and the ending. It is distinct from other sub-themes by focusing on the craftsmanship of the narrative elements themselves, rather than their integration into gameplay or world-building.

STORYTELLING.name: Story Engagement
STORYTELLING.definition: This sub-theme captures the player's engagement with the main and side stories, including the depth and consequence of the story, and the player's agency within it. It is distinct from other sub-themes by focusing on the player's emotional and intellectual engagement with the story, rather than the structural or thematic elements of the narrative.

STORYTELLING.name: World Building
STORYTELLING.definition: This sub-theme focuses on the creation and consistency of the game's fictional world, including its setting, atmosphere, and the integration of various elements into a cohesive universe. It is distinct from other sub-themes by concentrating on the spatial and environmental aspects of the narrative, rather than character or plot development.

STORYTELLING.name: Character Development
STORYTELLING.definition: This sub-theme pertains to the depth, complexity, and memorability of the game's characters, including their motivations, development, and the player's relationship with them. It is distinct from other sub-themes by focusing on the individual characters and their arcs, rather than the broader narrative or world-building elements.

MECHANICS.name: Combat Dynamics
MECHANICS.definition: This sub-theme focuses on the immediate interaction and overarching design of the game's combat system, including the feel, controls, variety, depth, balance, and player satisfaction. It excludes character progression elements, movement mechanics, and world interaction mechanics.

MECHANICS.name: Movement and Evasion
MECHANICS.definition: This sub-theme involves the mechanics of character movement, navigation, and evasion within the game world, including controls, hit detection, and strategies for avoiding combat. It is distinct from combat dynamics and world interaction mechanics.
example_codes: suggestion to use jumping instead of dodging

MECHANICS.name: Character Progression
MECHANICS.definition: This sub-theme covers systems related to character development, including skill trees, attributes, and progression mechanics. It is distinct from combat dynamics, movement mechanics, and world interaction mechanics.
example_codes: developers balance difficulty with character requirements

MECHANICS.name: Exploration and Resource Management
MECHANICS.definition: This sub-theme captures the player's experience with exploring the game world and managing resources, including crafting and inventory management. It is distinct from combat dynamics, character progression, and movement mechanics.

MECHANICS.name: Companion Interaction
MECHANICS.definition: This sub-theme focuses on the role and effectiveness of companions in the game, including their assistance in combat and exploration. It is distinct from character progression and movement mechanics.

CHALLENGE.name: Early Game Difficulty
CHALLENGE.definition: This sub-theme captures the initial challenge players face, focusing on the difficulty level and balance at the start of the game. It distinguishes itself from other sub-themes by specifically addressing the early stages of gameplay, where players often encounter steep learning curves and potentially unfair difficulty spikes.

CHALLENGE.name: Enemy Strength and Balance
CHALLENGE.definition: This sub-theme addresses the perceived power and balance of enemies throughout the game. It focuses on how enemy strength can impact player experience, distinguishing itself from other sub-themes by specifically examining the fairness and balance of enemy encounters, rather than the overall difficulty or combat mechanics.

CHALLENGE.name: Difficulty Curve and Scaling
CHALLENGE.definition: This sub-theme explores the progression and scaling of difficulty throughout the game. It is distinct from other sub-themes by focusing on how difficulty changes over time, including any spikes or inconsistencies, rather than the immediate challenge or enemy encounters.

CHALLENGE.name: Combat Challenge
CHALLENGE.definition: This sub-theme examines the difficulty and balance of combat mechanics, specifically focusing on how challenging combat is for players. It is distinct from other sub-themes by concentrating on the mechanics and execution of combat, rather than the broader difficulty or enemy encounters.

CHALLENGE.name: Overall Difficulty and Mastery
CHALLENGE.definition: This sub-theme captures the general perception of the game's difficulty and the sense of mastery players achieve. It distinguishes itself by addressing the overall challenge and the rewarding nature of overcoming it, rather than specific aspects like early game difficulty or combat mechanics.

PROGRESSION_CONTENT.name: Quest Diversity and Quantity
PROGRESSION_CONTENT.definition: This sub-theme focuses on the range and number of quests, including side quests, available for character progression. It is distinct from content volume by concentrating solely on the structure and availability of quests, without considering the overall content or progression mechanics.

PROGRESSION_CONTENT.name: Content Volume and Quality
PROGRESSION_CONTENT.definition: This sub-theme addresses the overall amount and quality of content available in the game, including undiscovered content and its engagement level. It is distinct from gameplay duration by focusing on the sheer volume and quality of content, rather than the temporal experience of playing the game.

PROGRESSION_CONTENT.name: Progression Speed and Reward Balance
PROGRESSION_CONTENT.definition: This sub-theme captures the speed of character progression and the balance between effort and reward. It is differentiated from character growth by focusing on the temporal aspect of progression and the satisfaction derived from rewards, rather than long-term character development.
example_codes: lack of ability progression for gear

PROGRESSION_CONTENT.name: Gameplay Duration and Engagement
PROGRESSION_CONTENT.definition: This sub-theme focuses on the length of gameplay and the player's engagement throughout the game's duration. It is distinct from content volume by emphasizing the temporal experience of playing the game, rather than the specific content or progression mechanics.

PROGRESSION_CONTENT.name: Character Growth and Replayability
PROGRESSION_CONTENT.definition: This sub-theme combines aspects of character growth over time with the game's replayability, highlighting how character progression and the game's design encourage multiple playthroughs. It stands apart from progression speed by linking long-term character development directly with the game's replay value.
example_codes: eventual completion of skill and stat progression

ONBOARDING.name: Learning Curve
ONBOARDING.definition: This sub-theme captures the difficulty and steepness of the initial learning process, focusing on how intuitive or challenging the game is for new players to understand its mechanics and rules. It is distinct from the general difficulty experienced after the player has learned the game, which falls under CHALLENGE.

ONBOARDING.name: Guidance and Direction
ONBOARDING.definition: This sub-theme addresses the presence or absence of guidance and direction provided to players at the beginning of the game. It focuses on how well the game directs players on what to do or where to go, distinguishing it from the lack of information in menus, which is categorized under UI.

ONBOARDING.name: Initial Gameplay Experience
ONBOARDING.definition: This sub-theme encompasses the overall experience of the early game, including its difficulty and how engaging or frustrating it is for players. It is distinct from the specific challenges faced during the initial hours, which are covered under a separate sub-theme.

ONBOARDING.name: Initial Experience and Engagement
ONBOARDING.definition: This sub-theme focuses on the initial engagement and overall experience of starting the game, including both positive and negative evaluations. It is distinct from the specific challenges of the initial hours, which are addressed separately.

ONBOARDING.name: Pacing and Progression
ONBOARDING.definition: This sub-theme addresses the speed and flow of the game's start, focusing on how quickly or slowly players progress and how this affects their initial experience. It is distinct from the specific challenges faced during the initial hours, which are covered under a separate sub-theme.

UI.name: Interface Design
UI.definition: This sub-theme encompasses the overall aesthetic and functional design of the user interface, including its layout, usability, and visual appeal. It is distinct from specific elements like controls or feedback mechanisms, focusing instead on the general design quality and user experience.
example_codes: interface design reminiscent of old software

UI.name: UI Clarity and Navigation
UI.definition: This sub-theme encompasses the clarity of the user interface and the ease of navigating and interacting with game menus, inventory, and quest systems, focusing on the cognitive load and user experience in accessing and managing game information.

UI.name: Feedback and Information Display
UI.definition: This sub-theme covers the adequacy and clarity of feedback provided to the player through the interface, including hit markers, character stats, and other vital information. It is distinct from the complexity or design of the interface, focusing on the presence and visibility of necessary information.
example_codes: lack of clear ui for character stats

UI.name: Control and Customization
UI.definition: This sub-theme involves the customization and responsiveness of controls, including keybindings and input methods. It is distinct from feedback and information display, focusing on how players interact with the game and customize their control schemes.

AUDIOVISUAL.name: World and Environment Visuals
AUDIOVISUAL.definition: This sub-theme encompasses the overall visual appeal and uniqueness of the game's world and environments, including the diversity and beauty of scenery, as well as any repetitive elements. It is distinct from general graphics quality and specific visual assets like character models.

AUDIOVISUAL.name: Graphics Quality
AUDIOVISUAL.definition: This sub-theme focuses on the technical quality and performance of the game's graphics, including resolution, texture quality, and overall visual fidelity. It is separate from the broader visual appeal of the world and specific animations.

AUDIOVISUAL.name: Visual and Animation Detail
AUDIOVISUAL.definition: This sub-theme addresses the intricacy and realism of visual details and animations, including texture quality, animation smoothness, and visual presentation. It is distinct from general graphics quality and the broader visual appeal of the game world.

AUDIOVISUAL.name: Sound and Music
AUDIOVISUAL.definition: This sub-theme covers the auditory aspects of the game, including the quality and impact of music, sound effects, and overall sound design. It is separate from the visual components of the game.

AUDIOVISUAL.name: Atmosphere and Ambience
AUDIOVISUAL.definition: This sub-theme pertains to the overall mood and immersive quality created by the game's visuals and sound, including lighting, weather effects, and environmental design. It is distinct from specific visual or auditory elements.

SYSTEM.name: Bug Impact Spectrum
SYSTEM.definition: This sub-theme encompasses the range of bugs and glitches in the game, from minor visual issues that minimally affect gameplay to major disruptions that significantly hinder game progression or stability.

SYSTEM.name: Crash and Stability
SYSTEM.definition: This sub-theme addresses the frequency and circumstances of game crashes, including crashes to desktop and during specific sequences. It is distinct from performance issues by focusing on complete game failures rather than frame rate or loading times, and does not include minor bugs or glitches.

SYSTEM.name: Technical Implementation
SYSTEM.definition: This sub-theme covers broader technical issues related to the game's programming and system requirements, including outdated technology and specific technical failures. It is distinct from bug frequency by focusing on systemic technical problems rather than individual bugs, and does not include minor or major bugs unless they are symptomatic of a larger technical issue.

SYSTEM.name: Save File Integrity
SYSTEM.definition: This sub-theme pertains to issues related to saving and loading game progress, including save file malfunctions and limitations. It is distinct from other technical issues by focusing specifically on save-related problems and does not include general performance or stability issues.

LIVE_DEVELOPMENT.name: Developer Resource Allocation
LIVE_DEVELOPMENT.definition: This sub-theme captures the perceptions and evaluations related to the allocation of developer resources, including time, effort, and attention, towards the game's development and post-release support. It distinguishes itself from other sub-themes by focusing specifically on the resources available to developers rather than the outcomes of their efforts or community actions.

LIVE_DEVELOPMENT.name: Future Improvement Expectations
LIVE_DEVELOPMENT.definition: This sub-theme encompasses the anticipation and hope for future improvements, balancing, and fixes by the developers. It is distinct from immediate developer responsiveness or specific patch content, focusing instead on the broader expectation of ongoing game enhancement over time.

LIVE_DEVELOPMENT.name: Patch and Bug Fixing
LIVE_DEVELOPMENT.definition: This sub-theme addresses the actions taken by developers to fix bugs and release patches, including the community's response to these fixes. It is differentiated from general development support by its specific focus on addressing game issues through patches.
example_codes: developer needs to fix game issues

LIVE_DEVELOPMENT.name: Update Frequency and Content
LIVE_DEVELOPMENT.definition: This sub-theme relates to the frequency and content of updates provided by the developers, including DLC and new features. It is distinct from patching and bug fixing by focusing on the broader scope of content updates and their timing.
example_codes: anticipation for updates and price drops

LIVE_DEVELOPMENT.name: Community and Mod Support
LIVE_DEVELOPMENT.definition: This sub-theme captures the role of community-driven mods and patches in enhancing the game experience, as well as the official support for such community efforts. It is distinct from developer-driven updates by focusing on the community's role in game improvement.
